question: On the Parallel Park (Conventional) exercise, the manual states you may be asked to park in a parallel parking space located where?
choice_a: On your right
choice_b: On your left
choice_c: Directly behind your starting position
choice_d: In an alley
explanation: The manual states, "You may be asked to park in a parallel parking space that is on your right."
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.5 Parallel Park (Conventional)

question: Before backing into the space during the Parallel Park (Conventional) exercise, how must you position your vehicle as you drive past the entrance?
choice_a: Perpendicular to the parking area
choice_b: Parallel to the parking area
choice_c: At a 45-degree angle to the space
choice_d: Facing directly into the space
explanation: The manual instructs you to drive past the entrance to the parallel parking space with your vehicle parallel to the parking area before backing in.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.5 Parallel Park (Conventional)

question: During the Parallel Park (Conventional) exercise, you must back into the space without crossing which boundaries?
choice_a: Only the rear boundary
choice_b: Only the side boundaries
choice_c: The front, side, or rear boundaries marked by cones
choice_d: There are no marked boundaries
explanation: The manual states you must back into the space without crossing front, side, or rear boundaries marked by cones.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.5 Parallel Park (Conventional)

question: To successfully complete the Parallel Park (Conventional) exercise, what must be true of your vehicle's final position?
choice_a: Only the front of the vehicle must be within the space
choice_b: The vehicle may remain partially in the traffic lane
choice_c: Only the rear wheels must clear the boundary
choice_d: The entire vehicle must be completely into the space
explanation: The manual requires that you get your entire vehicle completely into the space.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.5 Parallel Park (Conventional)

question: The Alley Dock exercise requires you to back your vehicle into an alley using what technique?
choice_a: Sight-side backing
choice_b: Blind-side backing
choice_c: Straight-line backing only
choice_d: Forward tracking
explanation: The manual states, "You may be asked to sight-side back your vehicle into an alley."
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.6 Alley Dock

question: Before backing into the alley during the Alley Dock exercise, how must you position your vehicle after driving past the alley?
choice_a: Perpendicular to the alley entrance
choice_b: Parallel to the outer boundary
choice_c: Facing away from the alley
choice_d: Already positioned inside the alley
explanation: The manual states you will drive past the alley and position your vehicle parallel to the outer boundary before backing in.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.6 Alley Dock

question: During the Alley Dock exercise, how close must the rear of your vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
choice_a: Exactly touching the rear boundary
choice_b: Within ten feet
choice_c: Within three feet
choice_d: Within one foot
explanation: The manual states you must back into the alley bringing the rear of your vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley without touching boundary lines or cones.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.6 Alley Dock

question: When you have completed the Alley Dock exercise, what must be true of your vehicle's position within the alley?
choice_a: It must be angled toward the outer boundary
choice_b: It may be at any angle, as long as it is inside the lines
choice_c: It must be touching the boundary lines
choice_d: It must be straight within the alley/lane
explanation: The manual states your vehicle must be straight within the alley/lane when you have completed the maneuver.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.6 Alley Dock

question: Which figure in Section 12 of the manual illustrates the Straight Line Backing exercise?
choice_a: Figure 12.1
choice_b: Figure 12.4
choice_c: Figure 12.3
choice_d: Figure 12.6
explanation: The manual captions Figure 12.1 as "Straight Line Backing."
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Figure 12.1

question: The manual illustrates two separate offset backing exercises. What are they labeled as in Figures 12.2 and 12.3?
choice_a: Alley Dock and Parallel Park
choice_b: Offset Back/Right and Offset Back/Left
choice_c: Forward Stop and Reverse Stop
choice_d: Straight Line Backing and Curve Backing
explanation: The manual captions Figure 12.2 as "Offset Back/Right" and Figure 12.3 as "Offset Back/Left."
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Figures 12.2-12.3

question: The manual depicts two different parallel parking maneuvers. Figure 12.4 shows Parallel Park (Driver Side); what does Figure 12.5 show?
choice_a: Alley Dock
choice_b: 90-degree Alley Dock
choice_c: Parallel Park (Conventional)
choice_d: Offset Back/Right
explanation: The manual captions Figure 12.4 as "Parallel Park (Driver Side)" and Figure 12.5 as "Parallel Park (Conventional)."
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Figures 12.4-12.5

question: During the on-road driving test, at all times you must do which of the following?
choice_a: Exceed the posted speed limit to keep pace with traffic
choice_b: Keep one hand off the wheel to signal at all times
choice_c: Drive only in the left lane
choice_d: Wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the test you must wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: To pass the on-road driving test, you must complete the test route without which of the following?
choice_a: An accident or moving violation
choice_b: Making any lane changes
choice_c: Stopping at any intersection
choice_d: Using turn signals
explanation: The manual states you must complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: According to the manual, "unsafe coasting" occurs when your vehicle is out of gear for longer than what?
choice_a: Five seconds
choice_b: The length of your vehicle
choice_c: One city block
choice_d: Ten seconds
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: If you are stopping behind another vehicle before making a turn, where should you position your vehicle to maintain a safe gap?
choice_a: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead
choice_b: At least two car lengths regardless of visibility
choice_c: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
choice_d: Anywhere within one lane width of the vehicle ahead
explanation: The manual states that if stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you (safe gap).
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: During the turn itself, what should you keep checking your mirror to make sure of?
choice_a: That the turn signal is still flashing
choice_b: That other drivers are yielding
choice_c: That the fuel gauge reading is accurate
choice_d: That the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn
explanation: The manual states you should keep checking your mirror to make sure the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: As you approach an intersection, if you must come to a complete stop, how should you do so?
choice_a: Without coasting, behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle ahead
choice_b: By coasting smoothly to a stop
choice_c: As close as possible to the vehicle in front of you
choice_d: Anywhere within the intersection itself
explanation: The manual states that if necessary, you should come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front of you.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, what does the manual specifically say you should not do?
choice_a: Check traffic thoroughly in all directions
choice_b: Change lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_c: Yield to pedestrians in the intersection
choice_d: Keep your hands on the wheel
explanation: The manual states you should not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the on-road test, where should your vehicle be positioned and how should your speed be managed?
choice_a: Centered in the left lane, below the speed of traffic
choice_b: Straddling the center line for better visibility
choice_c: Centered in the proper (right-most) lane, keeping up with traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_d: In whichever lane has the least traffic, at maximum legal speed
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: Before changing lanes during the multiple-lane portion of the on-road test, what should you do first?
choice_a: Signal only, without checking mirrors first
choice_b: Accelerate ahead of the vehicle in the target lane
choice_c: Sound the horn to alert nearby drivers
choice_d: Make the necessary traffic checks, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when safe
explanation: The manual states you should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: Once you are on the expressway, what three things must you maintain according to the manual?
choice_a: Proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed
choice_b: Radio volume, cabin temperature, and cruise control
choice_c: Constant acceleration, left-lane travel, and minimum following distance
choice_d: Four-way flashers, horn readiness, and parking brake engagement
explanation: The manual states that once on the expressway, you should maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once you are on the exit ramp when leaving the expressway, what must you continue to do?
choice_a: Accelerate to merge back into the main flow of traffic
choice_b: Decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles
choice_c: Activate your four-way flashers immediately
choice_d: Change lanes repeatedly to find the fastest path off the ramp
explanation: The manual states that once on the exit ramp, you must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: What situation is the Stop/Start maneuver intended to simulate?
choice_a: A railroad crossing stop
choice_b: A school bus student discharge
choice_c: Pulling your vehicle over and stopping as if you were going to get out and check something on it
choice_d: Merging onto an expressway
explanation: The manual states that for this maneuver you will be asked to pull your vehicle over to the side of the road and stop as if you were going to get out and check something on your vehicle.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Once your vehicle is fully stopped and safely out of the flow of traffic during the Stop/Start maneuver, which of the following must you do?
choice_a: Turn off the engine completely
choice_b: Leave your feet resting on the brake and clutch pedals
choice_c: Exit the vehicle immediately to inspect it
choice_d: Cancel your turn signal, activate your four-way emergency flashers, and apply the parking brake
explanation: The manual states that once stopped you should cancel your turn signal, activate your four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, move the gear shift to neutral or park, and remove your feet from the brake and clutch pedals.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume from the Stop/Start maneuver, what does the manual specifically say about the steering wheel?
choice_a: Do not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves
choice_b: Turn the wheel first, then release the parking brake
choice_c: Turn the wheel only once you have reached the speed of traffic
choice_d: The steering wheel should be locked straight for the remainder of the test
explanation: The manual specifically instructs: do not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When approaching a curve, when should you reduce your speed?
choice_a: While already inside the curve
choice_b: Before entering the curve, so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_c: Only after exiting the curve
choice_d: Speed reduction is unnecessary for gentle curves
explanation: The manual states that before entering the curve, you should reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: While any part of your vehicle is within a railroad crossing, what must you not do?
choice_a: Keep your hands on the steering wheel
choice_b: Check traffic in all directions beforehand
choice_c: Stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
choice_d: Decelerate before reaching the crossing
explanation: The manual states you should not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: If you are driving a bus, a school bus, or a vehicle displaying placards, at what distance from the nearest rail must you stop at a non-exempt railroad crossing?
choice_a: At least 100 feet away
choice_b: Exactly at the rail
choice_c: Within 10 feet of the rail
choice_d: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual states such drivers should stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: What may happen if your on-road test route does not include a railroad crossing?
choice_a: You may be asked to explain and demonstrate proper railroad crossing procedures at a simulated location
choice_b: You automatically receive full credit for that scoring category
choice_c: That portion of the test is skipped with no substitute
choice_d: The test must be rescheduled for a different route
explanation: The manual states that not all driving road test routes will have a railroad crossing, and you may be asked to explain and demonstrate the proper procedures at a simulated location.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass, the examiner may ask you to state what?
choice_a: The name of the overpass
choice_b: The posted clearance or height
choice_c: The number of support columns
choice_d: The posted speed limit ahead
explanation: The manual states that after driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: After going over a bridge, the examiner may ask you to identify what?
choice_a: The name of the waterway below
choice_b: The number of lanes on the bridge
choice_c: The posted weight limit
choice_d: The bridge's construction date
explanation: The manual states that after going over a bridge, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted weight limit was.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: As you stop a school bus for a student discharge, how far away from the students must you come to a complete stop, and what must you also do?
choice_a: At least 50 feet away; sound the horn twice
choice_b: At least 25 feet away; flash the headlights
choice_c: Exactly at the curb; leave the transmission in drive
choice_d: At least 10 feet away; place the transmission in neutral/park, set the parking brake, and activate the stop arm and red warning lights
explanation: The manual states the driver must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students, place the transmission in neutral/park, set the parking brake, and activate the stop arm and red warning lights.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: As you approach the student pick-up point, which warning lights and signal must you activate?
choice_a: Amber warning lights and the right turn signal
choice_b: Hazard flashers only
choice_c: Red warning lights and the left turn signal
choice_d: High-beam headlights only
explanation: The manual states that as you approach the student pick up, you must activate amber warning lights and right turn signals.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: Which of the following clutch practices does the manual specifically warn against?
choice_a: Using the clutch every time you shift
choice_b: Riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or "popping" the clutch
choice_c: Double-clutching on an unsynchronized transmission
choice_d: Returning both hands to the wheel after shifting
explanation: The manual states not to ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or "pop" the clutch.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: According to the manual's gear usage guidance, when should you avoid shifting gears?
choice_a: On straight sections of roadway
choice_b: While traveling uphill
choice_c: In turns and intersections
choice_d: While merging onto an expressway
explanation: The manual states not to shift in turns and intersections.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: According to the manual's brake usage guidance, how should you apply the brake?
choice_a: Pump the brake repeatedly for better control
choice_b: Use the parking brake for all routine stops
choice_c: Brake harshly to stop as quickly as possible
choice_d: Brake smoothly using steady pressure, without riding or pumping the brake
explanation: The manual states not to ride or pump the brake, and not to brake harshly; instead, brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.13(c) Brake Usage

question: According to the manual, where should a vehicle finish a left turn on a multiple-lane road?
choice_a: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_b: In the left-most lane available
choice_c: In any open lane
choice_d: Straddling both center lanes
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: According to the manual's steering guidance, where should both hands be at all times while driving?
choice_a: One hand on the wheel and one on the gearshift at all times
choice_b: On the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, then returned to the wheel once the shift is complete
choice_c: On the wheel only while actively turning
choice_d: It does not matter as long as the vehicle stays in its lane
explanation: The manual states to keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, and once you have completed the shift, return both hands to the steering wheel.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.15 Steering

question: According to the manual, when should you check your mirrors and traffic relative to an intersection?
choice_a: Only after clearing the intersection
choice_b: Only if another vehicle is signaling
choice_c: Before, while in, and after the intersection
choice_d: Only immediately before entering the intersection
explanation: The manual states you should check mirrors and traffic before, while in and after an intersection.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.16 Regular Traffic Checks

topic: On-Road Driving - Use of Turn Signals
question: According to the manual's guidance on turn signals, when should you cancel your turn signal?
choice_a: Only when another driver flashes their lights at you
choice_b: Ten seconds after activating it, regardless of completion
choice_c: Turn signals should never be cancelled manually
choice_d: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
explanation: The manual states you must cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: New Mexico CDL Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.17 Use of Turn Signals
